photographs.prompt:
Create one wide landscape documentary PHOTOGRAPH, approximately 2.1:1 landscape composition, for a British vegetable-growing book. Frame one of a pair: smothering weeds in John’s Cornish back garden. The action is instantly legible at a small printed size: John is kneeling at the side of a broad opaque dark bottle-green tarp, setting a single ordinary weathered brick down flat across the hem to keep it in place. His fingers actually grip its ends. The tarpaulin is already spread low and flat, directly on the whole cut-back weedy patch, small natural fabric creases, no frame or gap; a modest domestic rectangular patch, about 1.3 by 1.9 metres. Its perspective outline is readable including the front edge. Several other old dull bricks or heavy stones already weight it at corners and intervals along the perimeter. Grass surrounds the plot, no bare trench, no loose cut turves. John kneels on the grass beside the near/middle right-hand side, looking at the work, a natural three-quarter view of his face. In this shot the left two-thirds belongs to the tarp itself; show the working hands, brick and adjacent edge clearly against the green. The weighting action and material, rather than a posed portrait, are the subject.
Use reference 1 only for the actual man’s likeness (his high bare forehead, sparse close grey hair at sides, short greying moustache and beard, age, face shape); reference 2 for his medium build and plain charcoal pullover, dark blue everyday jeans, brown work shoes. Bare hands, no cap, no checks. Reference 3 shows John’s actual small aluminium greenhouse and its low masonry plinth, and reference 4 shows the colour and block texture of the pale grey-buff brick base. Reference 5 is a neighbouring book photo: borrow its photographic lighting, lawn, close working viewpoint, weathered rear fence and the low masonry wall beneath the fence. Move the camera and patch to the RIGHT in that garden. The BLUE SHED is entirely OUT OF FRAME. At the absolute RIGHT EDGE, behind the work, show only a small cropped sliver of the greenhouse side, daylight in its clear glass, thin aluminium glazing bar and a few courses of grey-buff brickwork beneath, to locate the action. Keep it on the right (roughly the last 6–9% of width) as a subtle clue only. No distant buildings, patio furniture, other beds, text, labels, tools left as props, decorative frame, watermark, illustrations or multiple panels. The back boundary is weathered vertical timber fencing on a low weather-marked light grey/buff masonry wall. Choose a slightly elevated view across and down on the grass so the patch, person and hands dominate almost the entire frame. Hard bed edging would defeat this example: this is just ground between lawn margins. Natural soft Cornish spring daylight, ordinary slightly damp grass and believable soil/weathering, documentary colour, natural hands and scale. Deliberately compose for a broad shallow crop across a printed page: keep his head, hands, ground action and small greenhouse base within the central 80% of image height, avoid useless foreground or sky. Deliver ONE full-bleed photograph only.

Create ONE landscape photographic image for print, 2.1:1 ratio, the LATER photograph of the same garden patch that is in reference 1. Keep that camera position, focal length, garden geometry, natural documentary colour, weathered low rear masonry wall with the vertical board fence directly above it, and a very narrow cropped side of the clear aluminium greenhouse on its pale brick base at the far RIGHT. No blue shed. The actor is John from reference 2 with the same likeness, receding hair, short greying beard, charcoal crewneck jumper, blue jeans and brown work shoes (reference 3 for clothes). Reference 4 shows the physical greenhouse; in this composition it must be only the small sliver at the extreme right as in reference 1. Your job is to photograph what happens weeks later when he has REMOVED the tarp after the cut weeds underneath it have died, and is now raking the dead growth off the ground.
On the SAME modest rectangular grass-surrounded footprint (left foreground and middle) as the tarp in ref 1, the viewer sees a wide patch of undisturbed, compact dark earth, still partly obscured by a thin, matted tangle of bleached beige lifeless grass stems and broadleaf weeds which have been starved of light. No dug trench or cut vertical edges, no loose turned clods, no planted crop, no tall upright weeds or growing green shoots on the patch. A small, visibly gathered loose windrow of dead stringy weeds is forming in the rake teeth; a few roots attached, and flattened straw-brown dead lawn still visible farther across. Clear in thumbnail: pale dead weeds against the brown earth and bright unmoved lawn fringe. The opaque dark forest-green tarp is fully OUT of the footprint, folded or rolled into a compact, slightly rumpled bundle on the grass, back LEFT beside the patch; the pieces of ordinary brick and stone that had weighted its edges are beside it out of his way, not left inside the bed. The bundle should be unmistakably the same cover, and small enough to leave the cleared surface legible.
John is now on his feet on the grass margin to frame right, knees bent and leaning forward, actually pulling an ordinary garden soil rake with both bare hands spaced down its single long straight wooden shaft. Angle the shaft diagonally inward from John at upper right toward a clearly visible traditional transverse steel rake head in the dead vegetation near centre. Show teeth facing down, touching and catching the dead stems; the steel rake head is across the end of the handle, one socket, no duplicate shafts. Position his upper hand only partway up the long handle so there is wood continuing naturally beyond it. Keep his face turned toward work, recognisable and visible in 3/4 aspect; just enough framing outwards if needed to fit his head and the action; do not add more setting. The rake and changing condition of the patch should be what the eye sees first. Camera looking slightly down. Realistic proportions and a believable gardening stance, ordinary overcast late-spring/summer light. The focus of the first photograph was a kneeling man weighting a tarp; THIS photograph must look distinctly different in his movement and the garden job: raking dead vegetation after removing all the cover. Exact same domestic site, perimeter, fence materials, greenhouse sliver on right and clothes. Shallow wide composition, no sky. Single full-bleed photographic shot without words, frames, diagrams, panels, staged props, or excess surroundings.
